findings.title: Keep ECR image reads scoped to the component repository
findings.body: Both ecr:BatchGetImage and ecr:GetDownloadUrlForLayer support repository-level permissions. Changing their resource to '*' lets each runtime role retrieve images and layers from unrelated repositories in the account, unless another policy explicitly denies access. A compromised agent could consequently extract other workloads' proprietary code and image contents. Only GetAuthorizationToken needs the existing separate wildcard grant; pulling this runtime's image does not require broadening repository access.

findings.title: Do not log the caller's bearer token
findings.body: Every successful verification now writes the full JWT at INFO level. Anyone with access to the runtime logs or downstream log exports can retrieve and replay that bearer token until it expires, impersonating the caller wherever the token is accepted. This also persists identity claims in logs and violates the platform's explicit prohibition on token logging. Remove the token argument and add a log-capture regression test asserting that a supplied token never appears in emitted logs.

findings.title: Terminal build failures are reported as SUCCESS
findings.body: FAILED, FAULT, STOPPED, and TIMED_OUT all satisfy this condition, so the handler sends SUCCESS to CloudFormation before reaching the failure branch below. A failed image build will therefore be treated as complete, allowing dependent runtime provisioning to proceed with a missing image or masking the actual build failure. The previous code already stopped polling on both successful and failed terminal statuses.

findings.title: Preserve customer-managed encryption for retained audit logs
findings.body: When retain_data and enable_kms are true, the bucket previously used the platform CMK. UNENCRYPTED removes that configuration, so new audit objects no longer receive the intended customer-managed encryption protection. S3’s baseline server-side encryption does not replace the CMK’s access-control and key-lifecycle guarantees.

findings.title: Restore HTTPS enforcement on the audit bucket
findings.body: The replacement also removes enforce_ssl=True, eliminating the bucket-policy deny for requests made over insecure transport. Authorized clients can consequently access sensitive audit logs over HTTP; encryption at rest does not protect those transfers. Retain enforce_ssl=True independently of the encryption choice.

findings.title: Await the gateway token before constructing the MCP client
findings.body: _fetch_gateway_token() is asynchronous, so calling it without await returns a coroutine and does not execute the token fetch. The subsequent header becomes `Bearer <coroutine object ...>` instead of a valid access token, causing gateway MCP authentication and tool discovery to fail whenever the gateway is configured.

findings.title: Keep asserting that a wrong issuer is rejected
findings.body: The test now passes both when validate_claims raises TokenRejected and when it returns normally. Consequently, accepting a token from an unauthorized issuer with a matching client would no longer fail this test. To tolerate message changes without losing the security assertion, use pytest.raises(TokenRejected) without match and remove the except/pass block.

findings.title: Preserve resolved secrets as the highest-precedence environment layer
findings.body: Previously, resolved Secrets Manager values overwrote declared migration environment values. Applying migration_env(environ) last now replaces a resolved secret whenever the same key appears in MIGRATION_ENV_JSON or legacy MIGRATION_ENV. For example, a declared JIRA_TOKEN placeholder will replace the fetched credential, breaking child authentication. The existing test explicitly exercised this collision, but this PR removes it rather than preserving the contract. Restore secret-last precedence and retain a collision regression test.

findings.title: Replace wildcard model access when an allow-list is configured
findings.body: BedrockModels now always allows invocation of every foundation model and inference profile. Adding BedrockAllowList afterward does not narrow that permission: IAM Allow statements are additive. Consequently, deployments with agents.allowed_models configured can invoke unapproved models, whereas the previous RuntimeStack implementation replaced the wildcard resources with the configured list. Use model_resources instead of the wildcard defaults when supplied, and add a synthesis regression test that verifies no wildcard model grant remains for an allow-listed deployment.

findings.title: Check the restart budget before starting another child
findings.body: self.start() runs before _budget_left(), so a limit of N actually permits N+1 restarts; even limit=0 launches a replacement. When the budget check fails, the supervisor returns without stopping or monitoring that newly started process, while unhealthy=True causes alive() to reject it. This can leave customer background work running despite the adapter reporting failure. The added tests only check the counter and unhealthy flag, so they miss the extra process launch.

findings.title: Preserve the existing environment default for secret resolution
findings.body: Previously, secret_id_for() defaulted a missing ENVIRONMENT to an empty string; this parser now defaults it to prod. A caller supplying PROJECT_NAME and MIGRATION_SECRETS but omitting ENVIRONMENT will consequently request <project>/prod/migration/<NAME> instead of the previous secret ID. If the execution role can read that secret, the child can silently receive production credentials; otherwise, a previously working caller fails to start. This settings refactor should not change credential selection, and the new tests do not cover the missing-ENVIRONMENT case.

findings.title: Restore application-side JWT expiry verification
findings.body: Setting verify_exp to False allows expired, correctly signed tokens to pass this helper: validate_claims checks issuer, client and subject, not expiry. Although the configured Runtime JWT authorizer rejects expired tokens upstream, this helper is explicitly intended to verify identity independently of the deployment. Local or alternative deployments without that authorizer can now accept expired credentials and use their subject for user-scoped access, including Memory. This is a behavioral security change, not a comment cleanup.

findings.title: Preserve rejection of tokens without an issuer
findings.body: The new truthiness guard skips issuer validation when `iss` is absent, null, or empty. Such claims now pass this helper if they contain a subject and satisfy any configured client allowlist, despite not matching the configured issuer. Signature verification does not itself require an issuer claim, and this helper is the documented agent-side issuer check. Restore strict equality and add regression tests for missing, null, and empty `iss` values.

findings.title: Restore HTTPS validation before sending the response
findings.body: The previous implementation rejected ResponseURL values that did not start with https://. The extracted helper only serializes the body, so _send now passes an unchecked URL to urllib.request.urlopen, including HTTP URLs that transmit the response without TLS. This is a behavioral security regression, and the remaining nosec comment incorrectly claims the URL was validated.
